title: acs v1: single-binary persistent ssh sessions
description:
Implement `acs` as designed in `docs/DESIGN.md`: one Rust binary that is the
local client, the per-connection remote proxy and the per-session remote
master, replacing the `dsh` shell function (ssh + dtach).

Invariants every child must preserve:

- Unfiltered stream: pty bytes reach the local terminal verbatim; keystrokes
  reach the pty verbatim except the command key (DESIGN §2, §6).
- Transport is the system `ssh`; no ssh-side configuration (DESIGN §3).
- Lossless resume after a network drop (DESIGN §5.2).

Done when every child is closed and DESIGN.md's Status reads Built.
close_reason: All 25 children closed: acs v1 implemented, tested on macOS and Linux, verified end to end over real ssh

title: Scaffold the acs crate: size-tuned profile, role dispatch, verify script
description:
Create the Cargo project the rest of the plan builds on (DESIGN §9).

- `Cargo.toml`: release profile `opt-level = "z"`, `lto = true`,
  `codegen-units = 1`, `panic = "abort"`, `strip = true`. Dependencies kept
  minimal: `rustix` (or `nix`) and `lexopt`; no async runtime, no clap.
- `src/main.rs`: role dispatch — default client; hidden `_proxy`, `_master`,
  `_install`, `_version`. Stubs are fine.
- Module skeleton per DESIGN §9 layout (`proto.rs`, `client/`, `master/`,
  `proxy.rs`, `install.rs`) and an `xtask/` workspace member placeholder.
- `scripts/verify.sh`: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`,
  `cargo test`, `npx markdownlint-cli2` on `**/*.md`.
- Flip DESIGN.md `Status:` to "In progress" and its CLAUDE.md index row, in
  the same change (repo convention).

Acceptance: `scripts/verify.sh` passes; `cargo zigbuild --release --target
x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` build; the slim
binary size for each target is recorded in the PR/commit message as the
baseline against the < 1 MB budget.
close_reason: Crate scaffold, size profile, role dispatch, verify script; slim release: x86_64-musl 320280 B, aarch64-musl 297928 B, aarch64-darwin 286080 B

title: Frame codec, message types and ACS-READY marker
description:
Implement the wire protocol of DESIGN §5.1 in `proto.rs`.

- Frame: `type u8 | len u32 BE | payload`. Hard maximum frame length
  (e.g. 1 MiB) rejected as a protocol error.
- Incremental decoder that accepts arbitrary read boundaries.
- All message types: HELLO (incl. client identity, `force`, TERM, COLORTERM,
  size, optional resume{instance, offset}), WELCOME (resumed/gap/fresh,
  created), BUSY, DATA (u64 offset), INPUT (u64 seq), ACK, RESIZE, PING/PONG,
  DETACH, KILL, EXIT, TAKEOVER, STATUS/STATUS_REPLY, ERROR.
- `PROTO_VERSION` constant; the `ACS-READY <proto>\n` marker and the
  `ACS-NEED <os> <arch>` line (DESIGN §3, §8): emit and a scanner that
  discards arbitrary preceding noise.

Tests: round-trip every message; decode with the input split at every byte
boundary; oversize and unknown-type frames error; marker found after
shell-rc noise and across split reads.
close_reason: proto.rs: frames, all message types, incremental decoder, ACS-READY/ACS-NEED scanner; 9 unit tests

title: Resume buffers: output ring with u64 offsets and input ack tracking
description:
Data structures behind lossless resume (DESIGN §4.2, §5.2).

- Output ring: append bytes, monotonically increasing u64 offsets,
  configurable capacity (default 1 MiB); `read_from(offset)` returns
  data / Gap (overwritten) / Future (invalid). Tracks the unsent watermark of
  the attached client so the master can apply backpressure.
- Input tracking: client-side queue of sent-but-unacked bytes (push, ack up
  to seq, iterate for resend); master-side dedupe that writes only the part
  of a resent INPUT beyond the last written seq.

Tests: wrap-around; gap detection exactly at the boundary; resend that
partially overlaps what the master already wrote is not duplicated.
close_reason: resume.rs: OutputRing (u64 offsets, gap/future, backpressure room), Unacked (client resend/rebase), InputDedupe (master); WELCOME gains input_seq; 9 unit tests

title: Command-key detector: Ctrl-] Ctrl-] then d (detach) / x (exit)
description:
Pure state machine for command mode (DESIGN §6.1-6.3), fed stdin bytes plus
an injected clock; outputs bytes to forward, actions (Detach, Exit) and the
next deadline.

- First Ctrl-] held up to 400 ms; a lone Ctrl-] or Ctrl-] + other key is
  forwarded as typed. Ctrl-] Ctrl-] within the window enters command mode;
  `d` / `x` act; any other key, or 2 s of nothing, forwards all held bytes.
- Recognise all encodings: legacy `0x1D`; kitty `CSI 93;5u` including event
  types `:1/:2/:3`; modifyOtherKeys `CSI 27;5;93~`. Consume whole escape
  sequences (never match inside one); buffer sequences split across reads;
  release events follow their press (forwarded or swallowed together).
- Bracketed paste (`CSI 200~` ... `CSI 201~`) passes through untouched.
- Escape key and window configurable (`ACS_ESCAPE_TIMEOUT_MS`).

Tests: table-driven `(bytes, timings) -> (forwarded, action)` covering every
rule above, including a pasted `^]^]d` and a terminal reply (`ESC`-prefixed)
arriving while a Ctrl-] is held.
close_reason: keys.rs Detector: legacy/kitty/modifyOtherKeys, releases, split reads, bracketed paste, passive replies/mouse, timeouts, configurable key; 20 table tests

title: Terminal mode observer and reset-on-detach sequences
description:
Passive scanner over the output stream that records which terminal modes the
remote program has turned on, and produces the matching resets for detach,
exit, or an abandoned reconnect (DESIGN §6.4). It must never modify, delay or
reorder the stream.

Modes: mouse (1000/1002/1003/1006/1015), bracketed paste (2004), alternate
screen (47/1047/1049), cursor visibility (25), focus events (1004), kitty
keyboard stack (`CSI > flags u` / `CSI < u`), modifyOtherKeys (`CSI > 4;N m`).

Tests: each sequence split at every byte boundary; reset output matches the
recorded state and is empty when nothing was set.
close_reason: modes.rs ModeObserver: DEC modes (mouse, paste, alt screen, cursor, focus, DECCKM, 2026), kitty stack/set, modifyOtherKeys, keypad, scroll region; ordered reset; 7 tests incl. every split point

title: Session names and per-uid socket directory
description:
Everything about where sessions live (DESIGN §4.1, §4.4, §4.5).

- Name validation `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`; default `main` or `$ACS_DEFAULT_SESSION`.
- Directory: `$ACS_SOCKET_DIR` or `/tmp/acs-<getuid()>` (never `$USER`,
  never `$TMPDIR`). Create `0700`; on existing path `lstat`: must be a real
  directory, not a symlink, owned by our uid, mode `0700` — else refuse with
  an error naming the owner and suggesting `ACS_SOCKET_DIR`.
- `sun_path` length check with a clear error.
- `flock` helpers for the per-session creation lock and the directory lock
  used by `--new` to pick the lowest free number.

Tests: symlinked dir refused; wrong mode refused; ownership check via an
injectable stat; too-long path; `--new` numbering with gaps and under
concurrent callers.
close_reason: session.rs: name rules, ACS_DEFAULT_SESSION, /tmp/acs-<uid> or ACS_SOCKET_DIR with symlink/not-dir/foreign-owner refusal and mode tightening, sun_path check, create/dir flocks, lowest free number; sys.rs libc wrappers; 13 tests

title: ssh command builder, option passthrough and remote prelude
description:
Build every ssh invocation (DESIGN §3, §7.1, §8).

- Session calls: transport options first (`-T -e none -o ControlMaster=no
  -o ControlPath=none -o ServerAliveInterval=0`), then the user's `-i`, `-p`,
  `-J`, `-F`, `-o` in the order given, then `[user@]host`, then the remote
  command. Side calls (`--list`, install) omit the transport options so they
  keep the user's multiplexing.
- ssh binary from `--ssh` / `ACS_SSH`, default `ssh` on PATH.
- Hidden `--transport-cmd <cmd>` that replaces ssh with a local command, for
  the integration harness (DESIGN §9.1).
- Remote prelude (POSIX sh) with the client version baked in: try
  `~/.local/share/acs/<v>/acs` then `/usr/local/lib/acs/<v>/acs`, `exec
  _proxy <session> <mode>`, else print `ACS-NEED $(uname -s) $(uname -m)`.
  Everything interpolated is shell-quoted (`-- command...` args are
  arbitrary).

Tests: argv snapshots for session vs side calls; precedence (a user
`-o ControlMaster=auto` comes after ours); quoting of hostile command args.
close_reason: ssh.rs: Transport argv (transport opts first for session calls, side calls keep multiplexing, user -i/-p/-J/-F/-o in order, -- before destination, ACS_SSH, --transport-cmd hook), sh_quote, versioned prelude run under sh -c; WELCOME carries session name; 7 tests incl. executing the prelude

title: Command-line parsing (dsh-compatible)
description:
`acs [ssh options] [user@]<host> [session] [-l|--list] [--new]
[--no-reconnect] [--force] [-v] [-- command...]` with `lexopt` (DESIGN §4.4,
§7, §7.1).

- `-r` accepted and ignored (reconnect is the default); `-l` is `--list`;
  ssh's `-l <login>` rejected with a hint to use `user@host` or
  `-o User=`.
- Invalid combinations rejected: `--list` with a session or `--new`;
  `--new` with a session name.
- `ACS_DEFAULT_SESSION` resolves the default session name.

Tests: table of argv -> parsed config / error message, including every
`dsh` invocation form.
close_reason: cli.rs: dsh-compatible parsing with lexopt; ssh -i/-p/-J/-F/-o passthrough in order; -r ignored; -l = --list with user@host hint; --new/--force/-v/--no-reconnect/--ssh/--transport-cmd; -- command; ACS_DEFAULT_SESSION; 8 tests

title: Master: daemon lifecycle, pty, child and peer-uid check
description:
`acs _master` process lifecycle (DESIGN §4.2, §4.5).

- Started by the proxy: double-fork, `setsid`, stdio to `/dev/null`; take the
  session creation lock; bind the socket **before** spawning the child;
  report readiness over a pipe (dtach's statusfd) so the proxy never races
  the bind.
- Child: `$SHELL -l` in `$HOME`, or the `-- command...` given; env `TERM`,
  `COLORTERM` from HELLO, `ACS_SESSION=<name>`.
- Reap the child on SIGCHLD, keep its wait status; unlink the socket on exit.
- Every minute re-check the socket path and re-bind if it was removed
  (tmpfiles cleanup).
- On every accepted connection verify the peer uid (`SO_PEERCRED` on Linux,
  `getpeereid` on macOS) and drop foreign uids.
- Instance id: random u64 minted at creation.

Tests: start a master in a temp `ACS_SOCKET_DIR` running `/bin/sh -c`; two
concurrent starts produce one master; child exit status observed; socket
removed on exit and re-bound after deletion.
close_reason: master.rs: spawn() with readiness pipe on fd 3, fork+setsid daemon, creation lock around check+bind, child on pty with setsid/TIOCSCTTY and TERM/COLORTERM/ACS_SESSION, SIGCHLD reaping, socket unlink on exit and re-bind after deletion, peer-uid check; tests: exit status, concurrent starts, rebind, missing session, protocol mismatch

title: Master: session protocol, takeover, resume, resize, kill
description:
The master's side of the protocol (DESIGN §4.2, §5.2, §5.3).

- HELLO handling with attach / create / attach-or-create; WELCOME with
  instance id and resumed / gap / fresh.
- One active client: a new attach sends TAKEOVER to the previous one.
- Output: pty reads go into the ring; DATA frames from the client's offset;
  backpressure while attached (stop reading the pty when unsent bytes would
  be overwritten); ring wraps freely while detached.
- Input: INPUT dedupe by seq, ACK.
- RESIZE via `TIOCSWINSZ`; on a fresh attach force a redraw by signalling
  `tcgetpgrp(pty)` with SIGWINCH even when the size is unchanged.
- PING/PONG; DETACH; KILL = SIGHUP to the child's process group, SIGKILL
  after 3 s; EXIT{status} to the client on child exit.

Tests (framed test client over the unix socket): resume from an offset
yields exactly the missed bytes; offset beyond the ring yields gap; a new
instance yields fresh; takeover; KILL kills a process group that ignores
SIGHUP; backpressure engages with a stalled client and not when detached.
close_reason: Master protocol verified by 10 integration tests: exact resume replay, gap and fresh attach, same-identity silent takeover vs BUSY + force, KILL SIGHUP then SIGKILL after 3s, backpressure for a stalled client and none while detached, resize, forced redraw on fresh attach, input dedupe

title: Proxy: connect-or-spawn master and relay frames
description:
`acs _proxy <session> <mode> --proto N` (DESIGN §3, §4.3).

- Resolve the socket directory; connect; on ENOENT/ECONNREFUSED unlink a
  stale socket and start the master (create modes only), waiting for its
  readiness report.
- Write `ACS-READY <proto>` to stdout before the first frame.
- Check the protocol version in the client's HELLO; on mismatch answer
  ERROR telling the user to finish or kill the session.
- Splice stdin/stdout <-> socket until either side closes.

Tests: stale socket replaced; two proxies racing to create converge on one
master; mismatched protocol version yields ERROR.
close_reason: proxy.rs: connect-or-start (retries when another master wins), ACS-READY, HELLO proto check, --new naming under dir lock, splice relay, --list; 7 integration tests via stdio incl. stale socket, racing proxies, mismatch, missing session, --new numbering, dropped client detaches

title: Session listing (--list) via STATUS
description:
`acs <host> --list` (DESIGN §4.3, §4.5).

- Master answers STATUS with name, attached/detached, attached identity (or
  last attached), creator identity, created-at, idle time, child command,
  size, acs version.
- `acs _proxy --list` enumerates `<dir>/*.sock`, queries each, reports and
  removes stale sockets; no `ps` parsing.
- Client prints an aligned table; `no sessions` when empty.

Tests: listing with attached, detached and stale sessions; output format.
close_reason: list.rs: side call to _proxy --list, STATUS_REPLY frames rendered as NAME/STATE/WHO/IDLE/AGE/COMMAND table, 'no sessions', not-installed case; tests: unit table + integration with attached, detached and stale socket

title: Client terminal: raw mode, guaranteed restore, signals
description:
Local tty handling (DESIGN §7).

- Raw mode with dtach's termios flags; the original termios restored on
  every exit path: normal return, SIGHUP/SIGTERM/SIGINT, and panic (drop
  guard plus signal handler, `panic = "abort"`).
- Self-pipe for signals; SIGWINCH surfaced as a resize event.
- Single-threaded `poll` loop skeleton with timers (escape timeout, pings).

Tests: termios flag computation as a unit test; a pty-based test that the
terminal is restored after the client is killed by a signal and after a
panic.
close_reason: tty.rs RawMode (dtach flags, suspend/resume) + emergency restore via panic hook and SIGTERM/HUP/QUIT/INT handlers; sys.rs termios/pty/poll/pipe/signal self-pipe/peer_uid/wait wrappers; pty-based tests prove restore after SIGTERM and after panic

title: Integration test harness: local transport, pty runner, producers
description:
Shared test infrastructure for everything end-to-end (DESIGN §9.1).

- Temp `ACS_SOCKET_DIR` and temp `HOME` per test.
- Run the client under a pty with `--transport-cmd` pointing at the built
  binary's `_proxy` (no ssh).
- Deterministic producers (numbered lines, binary patterns incl. escape
  sequences) and a byte-exact capture of the client's stdout.
- A framed test client for driving the master/proxy directly.
- Transport killer to simulate a network drop mid-stream.

Acceptance: a smoke test attaches, runs a producer, and asserts byte
equality of output; harness usable from `cargo test`.
close_reason: tests/common: Remote fixture (temp HOME with versioned install, socket dir, pid-recording transport wrapper to cut links), pty Client runner (keys, resize, wait_for, exit code), binary pattern producer; smoke tests prove prelude->proxy->master->pty chain byte-exact and ACS-NEED

title: Client: ssh transport, handshake and byte-exact session
description:
The client's session path without reconnect (DESIGN §3, §4.4, §5, §6, §7).

- Spawn ssh via the builder; sync on `ACS-READY` (discard noise, show it
  under `-v`); detect `ACS-NEED` and hand off to install.
- HELLO with TERM, COLORTERM, size; DATA written verbatim to stdout while
  tracking the last offset; stdin through the command-key detector into
  INPUT with seq; RESIZE on SIGWINCH.
- `d`: DETACH, restore terminal (with observer resets), print
  `acs: detached from <host>/<name> - reattach with: acs <host> <name>`,
  exit 0. `x`: KILL, wait for EXIT, exit with the child's status.
- On creating a session print `acs: new session '<name>' on <host>` on
  stderr before raw mode.
- Exit codes per DESIGN §7.

Tests (harness): attach-or-create, byte-exact output incl. escape sequences,
detach and re-attach, `x` ends the remote session, EXIT status propagated,
new-session message.
close_reason: client.rs: dial with marker sync, HELLO/WELCOME, raw mode, verbatim DATA with offset tracking, detector->INPUT with seq, RESIZE, d/x, new-session and reattach messages, mode resets, exit codes; 11 pty tests incl. 300 KB byte-exact output, detach/reattach, x, exit status, single-escape passthrough

title: Client: liveness, automatic reconnect and lossless resume
description:
Resume after network drops (DESIGN §5.2-5.4).

- PING after 3 s of silence; link dead after 10 s without a frame: kill ssh
  and redial with backoff 1 s -> 30 s, reset after a connection that lasted
  30 s. `--no-reconnect` disables.
- HELLO with resume{instance, offset}; handle resumed / gap (clear + redraw)
  / fresh ("session was restarted").
- Resend unacked input; drop keys typed while the link is known down, but
  keep command mode working (`d` detaches while down; `x` reports it needs
  the link).
- Status while disconnected: nothing for < 10 s; then one bottom-row line
  with save/restore cursor and the xterm title stack; one forced redraw
  after a resume that followed a status line.
- Cooked mode while ssh authenticates on redial (password / key touch).
- TAKEOVER ends the client with a message and the reattach hint.

Tests (harness): kill the transport mid-stream and assert the client's
stdout equals the producer's output byte for byte; input sent before the
drop is not duplicated; ring overflow while disconnected yields gap
handling; `--no-reconnect` exits on drop.
close_reason: reconnect.rs: Liveness (PING after 3s, dead after 10s), Backoff 1s->30s with reset, redial with resume, unacked resend, keys dropped while down but d works and x explains, status line + title stack, redraw via resize pair; 7 pty tests (cut, freeze, input once, --no-reconnect, detach while down, x needs link, gap) + unit tests; daemons close inherited fds

title: Client: immediate redial on network change
description:
Stretch goal from DESIGN §5.3: skip the backoff wait when the default route
changes (Wi-Fi switch, wake from sleep) — route socket / SCNetworkReachability
on macOS, netlink on Linux — where it is cheap to observe.

Tests: the reconnect scheduler redials immediately on an injected
"network changed" event.
close_reason: netwatch.rs: PF_ROUTE (address/interface messages only, ARP churn ignored) on macOS, NETLINK_ROUTE link/addr groups on Linux, FIFO injection for tests; offline wait redials at once on a change (max once per 2s) and resets backoff; unit tests + integration test (20s backoff bypassed)

title: Shared accounts: client identity and confirmed takeover
description:
Accident protection when several people use one remote account (DESIGN §4.5).

- Client identity `<local user>@<local hostname>`, overridable with
  `ACS_IDENTITY`, sent in HELLO; the master records attached and creator
  identities.
- Cross-identity attach gets BUSY{identity, since}; the client asks
  `take over? [y/N]` on the terminal, retries HELLO with `force` on yes;
  without a terminal it fails; `--force` skips the question.
- Same identity takes over silently (own dropped connection, own second
  terminal).

Tests (harness): same identity silent; different identity BUSY; force
takes over; non-tty without `--force` fails.
close_reason: Client identity (ACS_IDENTITY or user@host) in HELLO; BUSY answered with a cooked-mode [y/N] prompt naming who and since when, --force skips, non-tty declines; same identity silent takeover; ACS_DEFAULT_SESSION; 5 pty tests

title: Multi-user integration tests in a Linux container
description:
Prove isolation between Unix accounts (DESIGN §4.5, §9.1) in a Linux
container with two users (docker/podman; the macOS host cannot switch uids
without root).

- Another user's pre-created `/tmp/acs-<uid>` (squatted, and symlinked) is
  refused.
- A connection from another uid to a master's socket is dropped.
- Two users' `main` sessions are independent.
- The whole `cargo test` suite also runs on Linux musl in the container.

Acceptance: one script (`scripts/test_linux.sh`) runs it end to end.
close_reason: tests/multiuser.rs (squatted dir, symlinked dir, foreign peer uid dropped by master, independent per-user main) + scripts/test_linux.sh running the full suite on Linux musl and the multi-user tests as root with alice/bob; all pass. The Linux run found and fixed a master backpressure stall and a replaced-binary spawn failure.

title: Payload set: format, ELF trailer and Mach-O embed
description:
Carry slim remote binaries inside a complete binary (DESIGN §8.1).

- Payload set format: index of (target triple, compressed size, SHA-256,
  gzip bytes).
- ELF: trailer `[slim][P entries][index][magic + index offset]`, read back
  through `current_exe()`; writer used by xtask and by `_install --finish`.
- Mach-O: `embed-payloads` cargo feature using `include_bytes!` of a path
  supplied at build time.
- API: `own_target()`, `is_complete()`, `payload_for(target)`.

Tests: build a synthetic trailer and read it back; truncated or corrupt
trailer means slim, never a crash.
close_reason: payload.rs: blob format (gz entries + index + footer), build/parse, ELF trailer via current_exe, embed-payloads feature via include_bytes (build.rs ACS_PAYLOADS_FILE), own target (build.rs ACS_TARGET), uname->target map; dependency-free sha256.rs with FIPS vectors; corrupt/truncated input never panics

title: Remote self-install: ACS-NEED, versioned install, _install --finish
description:
Install `acs` on a remote on first contact (DESIGN §8, §8.1, §4.5).

- On `ACS-NEED <os> <arch>` map to a target. Case 1 (own ELF target):
  stream own file with `cat`. Case 2 (Linux target in P): stream gz(slim_r)
  to `gzip -dc > ~/.local/share/acs/<v>/acs.new.<token>`, then run
  `acs.new.<token> _install --finish --sha256 <digest>` with P on stdin,
  which appends the trailer, verifies the digest, renames to `acs`, and
  repoints `~/.local/bin/acs` (temp symlink + rename). Case 3 (macOS other
  arch): clear manual-install message.
- Random token per install so concurrent installs converge; missing `gzip`
  gives a clear error; side calls keep the user's ssh multiplexing; redial
  after install.

Tests (harness, local "remote" with temp HOME): install from slim fails
cleanly with the `cargo xtask dist` hint; complete binary installs and the
installed copy is byte-identical to the dist output for that target;
concurrent same-version installs converge; two versions coexist and each
serves its own client.
close_reason: install.rs: plan (self-copy for own target; gzip'd slim + payload blob for other Linux targets; clear errors otherwise), side calls, _install --finish (sha256 check, new file since running exe is ETXTBSY, atomic rename, ~/.local/bin symlink swap), once per run; --version lists installable targets; 6 integration tests incl. payload path via fake uname, concurrent installs, corrupt upload; verified dist binaries in docker

title: Prune unused remote versions
description:
Housekeeping from DESIGN §8: `_proxy` touches its version directory on
start; version directories untouched for 30 days with no running master of
that version (per STATUS) are removed at the next proxy start.

Tests: old unused version pruned; old version with a live master kept;
current version never pruned.
close_reason: prune.rs: proxy touches its version dir; at most daily (.pruned marker) removes other version dirs untouched for 30 days unless a live master reports that version (STATUS); unit test with backdated mtimes + integration test via proxy start

title: cargo xtask dist: slim builds, payloads, complete binaries, size budget
description:
Release build pipeline (DESIGN §8.1, §9).

1. Slim builds for `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin` (cargo) and
   `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`
   (`cargo zigbuild`).
2. gzip -9 the Linux slim builds into the payload set.
3. Complete Linux binaries by appending the trailer; complete macOS binaries
   by rebuilding with `--features embed-payloads`, then ad-hoc `codesign`.
4. Output `dist/<target>/acs` plus a size report; fail if slim > 1 MB or
   complete > 2 MB.

Acceptance: `cargo xtask dist` on this Mac produces all four; `codesign -v`
passes on the macOS ones; replace the size estimates in DESIGN §8.1 with the
measured numbers.
close_reason: cargo xtask dist builds 4 targets (zigbuild musl, native macOS), payload blob, complete Linux (appended) and macOS (embedded, ad-hoc signed, codesign -v ok), size report with budget; measured slim 473-602 KB, complete 1.10-1.21 MB; linux binaries verified in docker alpine (aarch64 native, x86_64 emulated)

title: Manual verification matrix against real hosts
description:
Check the things automated tests cannot (DESIGN §9.1) and record results
in `docs/VERIFICATION.md`.

- TUIs: vim (tag jump, mouse), Claude Code, htop, less; OSC 52 copy; a
  kitty-keyboard-protocol TUI (command key still works); local scrollback.
- Drops: `pfctl` block, Wi-Fi switch, laptop sleep/wake; output lossless.
- Install: macOS client -> Linux x86_64 and aarch64 hosts; Linux client ->
  next hop.
- Shared account: two identities, confirmation prompt.
- `-i` key selection against a host that needs it (e.g. corello).
close_reason: scripts/e2e_ssh.sh + tests/e2e_ssh.rs over real ssh to a container host: install on first contact, -i selection, vim, OSC 52/8, kitty command key, mouse, killed connection, frozen host, --list — all 9 pass; results and the hand-only checks (real terminal rendering, Claude Code, real Wi-Fi/sleep, corello) recorded in docs/VERIFICATION.md. Added ConnectTimeout=10 to the session transport.

title: Docs and migration from dsh
description:
Finish the rollout (DESIGN §10).

- `README.md`: install, usage, command keys, environment variables.
- DESIGN.md `Status:` -> Built, and its CLAUDE.md index row, in the same
  change.
- Migration note: run `acs` alongside `dsh`; then replace the `dsh` function
  in `~/.zshrc` with `alias dsh=acs` and drop the dtach dependency (the
  dotfile change is the user's to make).
close_reason: README.md (install, usage, command keys, ssh options, reconnect, shared accounts, environment, development scripts, dsh migration); DESIGN status Built; CLAUDE.md index rows for README/DESIGN/VERIFICATION and the test scripts; scripts/verify.sh passes

title: Automatic semantic versioning (scripts/version-bump.sh)
description: Bump the version automatically after each merge: PATCH for small fixes, MINOR for larger fixes and features, MAJOR only on explicit instruction (resets MINOR and PATCH). Reads unreleased commits since the last vX.Y.Z tag, updates Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock, pushes a chore(release) commit and tag to origin/main via a throwaway worktree. Run by the ship skill.
close_reason: cargo xtask bump + scripts/version-bump.sh: PATCH small fixes, MINOR features/larger fixes (>=300 shipped lines, Semver trailer or semver label), MAJOR only via --major (resets minor/patch); release commit + annotated tag pushed atomically from a throwaway worktree; idempotent; docs/VERSIONING.md; unit tests + end-to-end lifecycle test

title: Publish release binaries to GitHub Releases
description: Attach per-platform archives (acs-<version>-<target>.tar.gz), SHA256SUMS and install notes to a GitHub Release for each vX.Y.Z tag, built from the exact tag. scripts/release-binaries.sh does it; scripts/version-bump.sh calls it after cutting a release so shipping publishes binaries. Packaging lives in cargo xtask package (tested).

title: Add a YAML config file (/etc/acs, ~/.config/acs) with install_on_remote
description:
Add a YAML configuration file for the acs client.

User's ask: "add support for a configuration file, stored as YAML, using the latest unix directory standard, so local in ~/.config/acs/config.yaml as well as a global /etc/acs/config.yaml equivalent. If the global one exists, it is read first, overridden by the local one. Individual parameters override global, dictionaries and arrays are additive."

- Locations (XDG Base Directory): global `/etc/acs/config.yaml`, then local `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/acs/config.yaml` (default `~/.config/acs/config.yaml`). Either may be missing.
- Merge: the local file wins for scalars; dictionaries merge key by key (recursively); arrays concatenate (global entries first).
- First option: `install_on_remote` (bool, default `true`). When false, the ACS-NEED path (src/install.rs) does not install; it exits with a message saying acs is missing on the host and how to install it.
- `hosts`: a map of alias → list of entries `{host: string, user: string (optional), reachability_check: bool (default true)}`. This bead only parses and validates it; using it is the alias-resolution bead.
- A malformed file is an error that names the file and line, not a silent default.
- Nothing exists yet: no config code in src/, and today the only knobs are env vars (README "Environment").
- Binary size matters (budget 1 MB slim, DESIGN §9; deps today are only libc and lexopt). Choose between a small YAML crate and a hand-written parser for the subset used, and record the size cost.

Done when: both files are read and merged with those rules; `install_on_remote: false` stops a remote install; unit tests cover the merge rules, the defaults and error reporting; README and DESIGN document the file.
close_reason: Implemented: YAML config (/etc/acs, XDG local) with merge rules, install_on_remote, hosts parsing; hand-written YAML subset (+17 KB)

title: Add acs config subcommands to edit the configuration
description:
Add `acs config …` subcommands to manage the configuration file from the command line.

User's ask: "add options to the cli to allow configuration of acs through the command line, something like `acs config host add <alias> <hostname> --reachability-check`".

Proposed shape (settle the details during implementation):

- `acs config show`: prints the merged configuration and which file each value came from.
- `acs config get <key>` and `acs config set <key> <value>`, e.g. `acs config set install_on_remote false`.
- `acs config host add <alias> <host> [--user U] [--no-reachability-check]`: appends an entry, so repeated adds give an alias fallback hosts in order.
- `acs config host remove <alias> [<host>]` and `acs config host list`.
- Writes go to the local file (`~/.config/acs/config.yaml`); `--global` targets `/etc/acs/config.yaml` and needs the right permissions.

Notes:

- `config` becomes a reserved first argument. Today it would be read as a host name (src/cli.rs), so a host literally called `config` needs a way through, e.g. `acs -- config` or `user@config`. Document it.
- Writing must keep the file readable and stable (no reordering of what it did not touch); comments are nice to keep but not required.

Done when: every subcommand works against a temp HOME in tests; errors (unknown key, wrong type, missing alias) are clear; README documents it.

title: Resolve host aliases on connect with ping check and fallback hosts
description:
Resolve `acs <name>` through the configured host aliases, checking reachability and falling back to alternate hosts.

User's ask: "whenever connecting to a host, use the name as an alias if it is defined in the configuration. When it is, connect to the 'hostname', with user 'user' if defined (otherwise SSH will use its config). If reachability_check is true, use icmp ping once to check if the host is up. If it is, use it; if it is not, check the alternate 'host' if available. If not, display an error message and exit."

- Lookup: if the destination given to acs (without a `user@` part) is a key in `hosts`, try its entries in order.
- An entry with `reachability_check: true` is pinged once: `ping -c 1` with a short timeout. The timeout flag differs between macOS (`-t`) and Linux (`-W`). The first entry that answers is used. An entry with `reachability_check: false` is taken without a check.
- The chosen entry becomes the ssh destination: `user@host` if `user` is set, otherwise just `host`, so ~/.ssh/config decides the user.
- None reachable: print which hosts were tried and exit with the unreachable code (255, src/client.rs `code::UNREACHABLE`).
- Applies to every ssh call: session, `--list`, install. On a redial (src/reconnect.rs) the alias should be resolved again, so a fallback host is picked up after a network change. The master session stays the same only if the fallback is the same machine; say so in the docs.
- A name that is not an alias keeps today's behaviour exactly.
- `-v` should show which entry was chosen and why.

Done when: tests cover alias hit and miss, fallback to the second entry, `reachability_check: false`, all-unreachable → error/255, and `user` handling (ping is injected so tests don't need ICMP); README documents it.

title: Add a curl | sh installer for acs (per-platform install dir)
description:
Add a one-line installer: `curl -fsSL <url> | sh` installs acs the way the platform expects.

User's ask: "create an install script that someone can download which installs acs automatically according to the rules of the platform it is being installed on. Similar to other apps: `curl <something> | <some shell command>`."

Proposed design:

- `scripts/install.sh`, POSIX sh. It is also published as a release asset by `scripts/release-binaries.sh`, so the stable URL is `https://github.com/michel-onstein/acs/releases/latest/download/install.sh`. The repo is public.
- It maps `uname -s` / `uname -m` to one of the four release targets: macOS arm64/x86_64, Linux x86_64/aarch64. Anything else is a clear error.
- It downloads `acs-<version>-<target>.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS` from the release (latest by default; `ACS_VERSION=0.2.0` pins one) and refuses to install on a checksum mismatch. It uses `curl` or `wget`, and `shasum -a 256` or `sha256sum`.
- Install location follows each platform's rules: per-user `~/.local/bin` (XDG) by default, or `/usr/local/bin` when run as root or with `ACS_INSTALL_DIR`. It warns, with the line to add, when the directory is not on `PATH`.
- Re-running it upgrades in place, and it prints the installed `acs --version`.

Today install is manual: README "Install" has a curl + tar + install recipe, and the release assets exist since v0.1.0.

Done when: the script passes shellcheck; tests run it against a real release in Alpine and Ubuntu containers and in a temp HOME on macOS (default dir, pinned version, checksum failure, unsupported platform); README leads with the one-liner.

title: Check GitHub weekly for a newer acs release and show a message
description:
Check GitHub for a newer acs release once a week and tell the user.

User's ask: "have the acs binary check for a new release on github once a week, if a new release is available display a message".

Proposed design:

- Only the local client checks; the remote roles (`_proxy`, `_master`, `_install`) never do.
- At most once every 7 days, recorded in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/acs/update-check` (default `~/.local/state/acs/update-check`). It queries `https://api.github.com/repos/michel-onstein/acs/releases/latest` and compares `tag_name` to our version with semver.
- acs has no HTTP/TLS client, and adding one would break the 1 MB size budget (DESIGN §9). So it shells out to `curl` with a short timeout (for example `-m 3`) and never blocks or delays connecting: run it in the background and show the result on the next start, or finish within the timeout before raw mode.
- The message goes to stderr outside the session stream, e.g. `acs 0.3.0 is available (you have 0.2.0) — run: acs upgrade`. It is shown once per new version, not on every run.
- Can be turned off with `ACS_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`, and with an `update_check: false` option once the YAML config file (acs-xfk) exists. Being offline or rate-limited stays silent.

Done when: unit tests cover the interval, the version comparison and the "shown once" state; an integration test injects the API response (e.g. a fake curl on PATH); README documents it and how to turn it off.

title: Add acs upgrade: self-upgrade from GitHub releases
description:
Add `acs upgrade`: replace the running acs with the latest (or a given) GitHub release.

User's ask: "add ability to do a self upgrade (from github)".

Proposed design:

- `acs upgrade [--version X.Y.Z] [--check]`. `upgrade` becomes a reserved first argument, like `config` in acs-iff.
- It finds the latest release (or the given one), downloads `acs-<version>-<own target>.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS` via `curl` (acs has no HTTP/TLS client; DESIGN §9 size budget), and verifies the checksum.
- It replaces the binary behind `current_exe()` atomically: write a temp file next to it, then rename it into place, keeping the mode. If that directory is not writable (e.g. `/usr/local/bin`), it says to re-run with sudo.
- It refuses a downgrade unless `--version` asks for it, and does nothing when already current. `--check` only reports.
- Remote hosts need nothing: the next connection finds no binary for the new version and installs it (versioned install, DESIGN §8).
- On macOS, a curl download carries no quarantine attribute; the ad-hoc signature must still verify after the rename.
- The download-and-verify logic should match the one-line installer (same asset names), so the two agree.

Done when: tests cover upgrading from a fake release server or injected curl (success, checksum mismatch, already current, unwritable directory), a real upgrade from v0.1.0 → latest is exercised once, and README documents `acs upgrade`.

title: Fix payload install failing when the login shell prints to stdout
description:
Step 1 of the payload install plan (`gzip -dc > tmp`, src/install.rs ~L114) prints nothing, and `side_call` (src/install.rs ~L150) errors with "unexpected reply while installing" whenever stdout is non-empty and no line is exactly `ok`. Any `.bashrc` echo or motd script that writes to stdout for non-interactive sessions — the very noise the ACS-READY marker was designed to tolerate (DESIGN §3) — therefore fails the macOS → Linux self-install after the upload succeeded, leaving `acs.new.<token>` behind. The self-copy path only passes because the finisher happens to print `ok`.

Done when the upload step is judged on exit status alone (or prints its own marker) and tests/install.rs has a case with a chatty login shell.

title: Stop link_bin clobbering or downgrading ~/.local/bin/acs
description:
`link_bin` (src/install.rs ~L279) creates a symlink to the version just installed and renames it over `~/.local/bin/acs` unconditionally. Consequences: a hand-installed regular file there (what the release notes tell users to `install -m 755`) is replaced by a symlink into `~/.local/share/acs/<v>/`; an older client connecting to a host with a newer version installed silently downgrades the host's link (DESIGN §8 says it points at the *newest* installed version); a later prune of that version leaves the link dangling.

Done when the link is only replaced if absent or a symlink into `~/.local/share/acs/`, and only when the target version is >= the one it currently points at, with a test for a pre-existing file and a pre-existing newer symlink.

title: Fix master dropping the child's final output at exit (stale revents)
description:
The "pty drained" check (src/master.rs ~L453-458) decides from the revents of the poll that just returned: if the child has been reaped, POLLIN was requested and the pty did not report POLLIN, `pty_open = false` and the next iteration goes to `finish()` without reading the pty again. But `sys::poll` maps EINTR to `Ok(0)` with all revents zero, and SIGCHLD is installed without SA_RESTART, so the child's own exit interrupts the poll; `reap()` then sets `status` and the same iteration closes the pty. On Linux a slave write reaches the master's read queue asynchronously (flip buffer → workqueue), so `echo done; exit` can lose its last line. The same happens when poll returned for another fd and the child wrote and exited before `reap()` ran.

Done when the drained decision requires a subsequent quiet poll of the pty *after* the status was observed (e.g. the full 50 ms timeout genuinely expiring), and a regression test exercises output-then-exit repeatedly.

title: Bound dial and the HELLO→WELCOME handshake with a deadline
description:
`dial()` (src/client.rs ~L124-170) reads the ssh pipe with a plain blocking `read` — no poll, no deadline, the signal fd is not watched — and `serve()` uses `timeout = -1` and only starts `Liveness` after the first WELCOME (~L551, L639). ssh's own keepalive is disabled by design (ServerAliveInterval=0) and ConnectTimeout=10 only covers TCP connect. A redial whose connect succeeds but then stalls (half-alive host, firewall that accepts and blackholes, a wedged remote before WELCOME) hangs the client until Ctrl-C. The 10 s dead-link guarantee of DESIGN §5.3 has a hole exactly in the reconnect path. A login file with `printf` and no trailing newline (see the marker bead) triggers the same hang deterministically.

Done when the marker wait and the handshake are covered by a deadline (poll-based, with the signal fd), a timed-out redial returns to backoff, and a test with a silent remote proves it.

title: Pop the title stack and status line when the session ends during an outage
description:
After a link drop, `offline()` (src/reconnect.rs ~L207-219) draws the bottom status row and pushes the xterm title (`CSI 22;0 t`), setting `status_shown`. The pop (`clear_status`) only runs from `on_welcome` and the offline Detach path. If the redial gets `Error{NO_SESSION}`, `Exit`, or `Takeover` before any WELCOME (src/client.rs ~L487-529), `serve` returns and `run()` calls only `leave()` (~L301), which never pops. The terminal keeps the "acs: host — connection lost" title and the inverse-video status row after acs exits — a DESIGN §5.4 violation. tests/reconnect.rs only covers the detach-while-down path.

Done when `leave()` (or those return paths) calls `clear_status` whenever `status_shown`, with a test for session-end-during-outage.

title: Fix proxy busy-spin after client EOF while input is backpressured
description:
In `relay()` (src/proxy.rs ~L217-225) once stdin hits EOF `stdin_open = false` and its pollfd gets `events = 0`, but poll reports POLLHUP on a closed pipe regardless of `events`. Every iteration then returns immediately from poll, reads 0, and loops, for as long as `to_master` cannot drain — which is exactly when the master has stopped reading (PTY_IN_HIGH_WATER, child not consuming input). Trigger: paste a lot into a program not reading stdin, then the ssh connection drops → the proxy spins at 100 % CPU until the child reads or the session ends.

Done when the stdin pollfd uses `fd = -1` once closed (poll ignores negative fds), with a backpressure test in tests/proxy.rs.

title: Fix master spinning on pty POLLHUP while the ring is full
description:
With an active client stalled and the ring full (`room_before_overwrite(next) == 0`) the master polls the pty with `events = 0` (src/master.rs ~L384-395), but Linux `n_tty_poll` reports POLLHUP once the slave side closes, regardless of `events` and even with unread data. Poll then returns immediately, `read_pty` bails at `want == 0` (~L793-796), the drained heuristic does not apply because `asked` is false, `pump_output` cannot add (client at high water), and the loop spins hot until the client drains a chunk or the connection dies. Trigger: `acs host -- cat big.log` over a stalled link when cat finishes.

Done when the pty fd is omitted from the poll set (or the loop sleeps) while `room == 0`, with a test covering hangup-while-stalled.

title: Ignore frames from a taken-over or detached (Closing) connection
description:
`handle()` (src/master.rs ~L553-591) has no check for `ConnState::Closing`. A Closing conn is not polled for POLLIN, but POLLHUP is always reported, so when the old client's proxy closes, `read_conn` decodes whatever was still buffered and applies it as for the active client: INPUT goes to the pty and advances `InputDedupe::written`, so the new client's first keystrokes at the same sequence are dropped as duplicates (DESIGN §5.1 says clients taking turns never collide); RESIZE resizes the new client's pty; KILL kills the session. Trigger: the old client types or resizes between the takeover and its exit on TAKEOVER, or its proxy holds unsent input when the link died.

Done when Closing conns are drained without handling (or skipped in read_conn), with a test that a late INPUT/RESIZE/KILL from a taken-over conn is ignored and the new client's input_seq stays consistent.

title: Guard against tcgetpgrp returning 0 so hard_kill cannot kill the master
description:
Linux `tiocgpgrp` on a pty *master* fd returns `pid_vnr(real_tty->ctrl.pgrp)`, which is 0 when the slave has no foreground group (after TIOCNOTTY, after a hangup, or during the leader's exit between `disassociate_ctty()` and reaping). `hard_kill` (src/master.rs ~L886-888) only filters `p != ch.pid`, so `kill(-0, SIGKILL)` == `kill(0, SIGKILL)` signals the master's own process group — the master is a session leader after setsid, so it dies and takes the user's session with it. `start_kill` (~L871) and `resize` (~L772) hit the same value harmlessly. Rare (child ignores SIGHUP and dropped its ctty, or exits at the 3 s deadline) but the consequence is total.

Done when every tcgetpgrp result is filtered with `p > 0`, with a unit test on the filter.

title: Only prune version directories under $HOME/.local/share/acs
description:
`versions_root()` (src/prune.rs ~L31-38) is `parent(parent(current_exe))` whenever the parent dir is named after the version, with no check that it lies under `$HOME`. A binary exec'd from the prelude's second candidate, `/usr/local/lib/acs/<v>/acs` (src/ssh.rs ~L107), therefore touches `/usr/local/lib/acs/<v>`, writes `/usr/local/lib/acs/.pruned`, and `remove_dir_all`s other users' system-wide versions older than 30 days that are not in *this user's* live set. Silent for a non-root user (errors ignored) but effective for root or wherever `/usr/local/lib` is user-writable (Homebrew on Intel macOS). DESIGN §8 says acs never writes there.

Done when pruning only runs with `root == $HOME/.local/share/acs`, with a test that a system-path binary prunes nothing.

title: Take the create lock before --list removes a stale socket
description:
`list()` (src/proxy.rs ~L317-325) removes a socket after ECONNREFUSED/ENOENT without holding `create_lock`, while master start (src/master.rs ~L304-315) does check → unlink → bind under that lock. Interleaving: list connects (refused, old stale file) → master A unlinks the stale file and binds a fresh socket → list unlinks A's *live* socket. A is unreachable for up to `rebind_every()` (60 s); any proxy in that window spawns master B; when A's `check_socket` runs it sees another inode and leaves it — A is orphaned forever with its shell still running.

Done when the refused → unlink step takes `dir.create_lock(name)` (try_lock; skip if busy), with a test for list racing a bind.

title: Drain queued output to the client before failing on a master write error
description:
In `relay()` (src/proxy.rs ~L266) `flush(m, &mut to_master)?` propagates EPIPE when the master closed between this iteration's `read(m)` — which just queued the EXIT frame into `to_client` — and the write. `session()` then errors out without `drain(STDOUT, &to_client)`, so the client sees "link lost" and later NO_SESSION instead of the child's exit status. Needs queued client input (a PING or INPUT) in the same iteration, so the window is narrow.

Done when a write error to the master falls through to the drain path instead of `?`, with a test for EOF-with-pending-output ordering.

title: Emit a newline before the ACS-READY/ACS-NEED marker so printf noise cannot swallow it
description:
`parse_marker` (src/proto.rs ~L636) requires the marker to start a line. A `printf "foo"` (no `\n`) in a startup file makes the line `fooACS-READY 1` / `fooACS-NEED ...`, which is rejected. For ACS-NEED the client reports "the connection closed before acs started"; for ACS-READY the client blocks in `dial` waiting for a marker while the proxy blocks waiting for HELLO — a mutual hang with no timeout on either side (see the dial-deadline bead).

Done when `ready_line()` and the prelude's `printf` (src/ssh.rs) emit a leading `\n`, with a scanner test for noise without a trailing newline.

title: Honour ACS_ESCAPE_TIMEOUT_MS in the offline command-key detector
description:
`client_escape()` (src/reconnect.rs ~L194-203) copies only ACS_ESCAPE_KEY into the detector config used while the link is down; `escape_config()` (src/client.rs ~L74-89) reads both ACS_ESCAPE_KEY and ACS_ESCAPE_TIMEOUT_MS. A user with a custom escape window who double-taps Ctrl-] d during an outage gets the hard-coded 400 ms window instead, so the timing silently differs while disconnected.

Done when both sites share one config constructor and a test asserts the offline detector uses the configured window.
